raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview When the Parser Engine rejects a tool call, streaming kept emitting later calls at their raw slot index. The first valid call then streams as `index: 1`, which crashes the OpenAI SDK's stream helper and, with `parallel_tool_calls=False`, drops the call entirely. This PR streams each call at its position in the non-streaming result. Two cases trigger the rejection: an undeclared tool name with `validate_tool_names`, and a malformed Kimi call id. Fixes #63581. ## Claims - Streamed `tool_calls[].index` now matches the call's position in the non-streaming result when an earlier call is rejected. In production that affects `glm47` and `minimax_m2` (undeclared tool names) and `kimi_k2` (malformed call ids). With `validate_tool_names` forced on, every engine parser in the replay suite shows the same gap: 13 parsers, including Qwen3 (see #50986). The new cross-parser test covers parsers that enable validation later. - The OpenAI Python SDK stream helper (`ChatCompletionStreamState`) no longer raises `IndexError` on these streams. - With `parallel_tool_calls=False`, the streamed response now contains the valid call instead of no tool call. - No change when no call is rejected: the remap is the identity. ## Validation New tests, run on `main` (fix reverted) and on this branch: ```bash VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -q \ "tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py::TestRejectedToolCallIndex" \ "tests/tool_parsers/test_kimi_k2_tool_parser.py::TestStreamingHappyPath::test_streaming_matches_nonstreaming" ``` ```text # main E assert {1} == {0} E AssertionError: Incorrect index for tool delta. Got 1, expected 0 # 26x TestRejectedToolCallIndex (13 parsers x chunk1/chunkNone), 1x kimi_k2[invalid_id_skipped] 27 failed, 3 passed # this PR 30 passed ``` `TestRejectedToolCallIndex` (suggested in review by @smiyamoto3) takes each replay parser's two-call sample and declares only the second tool. It forces `validate_tool_names=True` and checks that the streamed indices are `{0}` and match `parse()`. It asserts the indices directly because `collect_output` groups calls by index and drops the index itself. That is why the existing replay tests missed the gap. `deepseek_v32` has no two-call sample, so it is not covered. The Kimi case covers the malformed-id path, which runs with validation off. End to end through the composed `Parser` the server uses (`ParserManager.get_parser("glm47", ...)`, `parse_delta(..., finished=...)`, one token per delta, real GLM-4.7 tokenizer), with the chunks fed into the OpenAI SDK. The script is in the linked issue. | | `main` | this PR | |---|---|---| | streamed index of the valid call | `1` | `0` | | `openai` 3.37.0 `ChatCompletionStreamState` | `IndexError: list index out of range` | `get_weather {"city": "Beijing"}` | | `parallel_tool_calls=False`, streaming | `[]` (call lost) | `get_weather {"city": "Beijing"}` | | `parallel_tool_calls=False`, non-streaming | `get_weather` | `get_weather` (unchanged) | MiniMax-M2 (real tokenizer) shows the same before/after. Regression suites on CPU: ```bash VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -q tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning # 9309 passed, 1 skipped, 30 xfailed ``` `pre-commit` passes on the changed files. CI: both tests run in the existing CPU steps "(CPU) Params, Env, Tokenizers, Parser" (`pytest parser`) and "(CPU) Tool Parsers", whose `source_file_dependencies` include `vllm/parser/`. No model evaluation: the change only renumbers streamed tool-call deltas, and only when a call was rejected. Generated tokens and non-streaming output are unchanged. ## Details **Root cause.** The engine opens one `ToolCallSlot` per call the model starts. The delta builders (`_emit_name_delta`, `_handle_arg_chunk`, `_handle_tool_end`, and Kimi's `_handle_arg_chunk` override) all stream `index=`. A slot whose name is rejected never sets `name_sent`, and `_build_extracted_result` skips it, so non-streaming compacts while streaming leaves a gap. **Fix.** In `_events_to_delta`, every streamed tool-call delta passes through one place before coalescing. There, set each delta's index to the number of earlier slots with `name_sent`. This is safe because calls stream in order: when slot `i` emits, each earlier slot is already final, either sent or rejected. Internal state stays keyed by slot index; only the outgoing delta changes. `_coalesce_tool_call_deltas` merges by index, and the mapping is one-to-one on sent slots. **Other consumers of the index** keep working: Responses API grouping (`streaming_events.py`), the Anthropic and Cohere index-to-id maps, and `maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls`, which this fixes. All of them either key by index or expect 0-based positions. **Interaction with #50986.** That open PR enables `validate_tool_names` for Qwen3 and adds `test_invalid_name_is_filtered_and_valid_call_keeps_raw_index`, asserting the gapped `index == 1`. With this change, that assertion would become `{0}`. I think 0 is correct, because it matches non-streaming and OpenAI clients, but I'm flagging it for whoever reviews both. cc @c5566b **Not a duplicate.** I searched open issues and PRs for "tool call index", "validate_tool_names", "undeclared tool streaming", "kimi_k2 invalid", "rejected tool call index" and "non-contiguous index". The only related item is #50986 above, which pins the current behaviour rather than changing it. **Limitation.** There is no `RemoteOpenAIServer` test. The affected checkpoints (GLM-4.7, MiniMax-M2, Kimi-K2) are far too large for CI or local hardware, and no small model uses a name-validating engine parser. Validation instead goes through the same `Parser.parse_delta` path the server calls, plus the real OpenAI SDK, as shown above. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
**AI assistance:** Claude (Claude Code) was used to find the bug (a streaming-vs-non-streaming differential sweep over the parser test suites), write the repro, and draft the fix, tests and this description. 💬 Join our developer Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai to discuss your PR in `#pr-reviews`, coordinate on features in `#feat-` channels, or join special interest groups in `#sig-` channels.

PRs do not trigger a full CI run by default. Reviewers with write access and configured trusted contributors can comment `/ci run` for upstream CI or `/amd-ci run` for AMD CI only whenever CI signals are needed.

Once the PR is approved or has the `ready` label, the PR author can also use the corresponding `/ci run`, `/ci retry`, and `/ci cancel` commands, or their `/amd-ci` variants. New commits do not start upstream CI automatically.

🚀

Thanks for the review! I added `TestRejectedToolCallIndex` to `tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py`, as you suggested.

For every `_PARSERS` entry, it takes the `think-then-parallel-tools` sample and declares only the second tool. It then forces `validate_tool_names=True` on the parser's config and checks two things: the streamed tool-call indices are `{0}`, and the streamed calls match `parse()`.

- On `main` (fix reverted), all 26 cases fail with `assert {1} == {0}`. That's 13 parsers (Qwen3, DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Gemma4, GLM-4.7, Granite-thinking, Kimi-K2, MiMo, MiniMax-M2, Nemotron V3 x2, Seed-OSS, Step3.5) at two chunk sizes: one token per delta, and the whole output at once.
- With the fix, all 26 pass.

The existing replay tests missed this because `collect_output` / `accumulate_deltas` groups calls by `tc.index` and returns only the values. A stream that starts at index 1 therefore looks identical to a correct one, so the new test asserts the indices directly.

Since this covers MiniMax-M2, I dropped the MiniMax-specific test. I kept the Kimi case in `test_kimi_k2_tool_parser.py`, because it covers the malformed-call-id path, which runs with name validation off. `deepseek_v32` has no two-call sample in `trace_builder`, so it isn't covered by this test.

@smiyamoto3 would you please review again!! much appreciated. Thanks

I think the fix is right.

The description describes it also covers any engine parser that later enables `validate_tool_names`. Could you add new test for that in `tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py`? 
Parametrizing over `_PARSERS` with `validate_tool_names` forced on and an undeclared call first catches this on main for every parser there.

files.patch:
@@ -497,6 +497,58 @@ def test_parse(self, parser_cls, sample, think_end, tool_start):
         )
 
 
+_PARALLEL_SAMPLES = [
+    (p.parser_cls, s)
+    for p in _PARSERS
+    for s in p.samples
+    if s.id.endswith("-think-then-parallel-tools")
+]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("chunk_size", [1, None], ids=lambda c: f"chunk{c}")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "parser_cls,sample",
+    _PARALLEL_SAMPLES,
+    ids=lambda v: v.id if hasattr(v, "id") else getattr(v, "__name__", ""),
+)
+class TestRejectedToolCallIndex:
+    """A call rejected by name must not shift the streamed index of later calls.
+
+    Only the second of two parallel calls is declared and name validation is
+    on, so non-streaming returns that call alone, at position 0.
+    """
+
+    def test_streamed_index_matches_non_streaming(self, parser_cls, sample, chunk_size):
+        declared = [t.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for t in sample.tools[1:]]
+
+        def make_parser():
+            parser = _make_parser(parser_cls, make_mock_tokenizer(sample), sample)
+            # Force validation on for every parser, not only those enabling it.
+            parser.parser_engine_config = dataclasses.replace(
+                parser.parser_engine_config, validate_tool_names=True
+            )
+            return parser
+
+        expected = parse_non_streaming(
+            make_parser(), sample, _test_request(tools=declared)
+        )
+        deltas = replay_streaming(
+            make_parser(),
+            sample.tokens,
+            chunk_size=chunk_size,
+            finished_on_last=True,
+            tools=declared,
+            prompt_token_ids=sample.prompt_token_ids,
+        )
+
+        assert [tc["name"] for tc in expected.tool_calls] == [
+            sample.expected_tool_calls[1]["name"]
+        ]
+        # collect_output groups calls by index, so check the indices directly.
+        assert {tc.index for d in deltas if d for tc in d.tool_calls} == {0}
+        assert collect_output(deltas).tool_calls == expected.tool_calls
+
+
 _WS_TOOL_SAMPLES = [(t[0], t[1]) for t in _TOOL_CALL_SAMPLES if "whitespace" in t[1].id]

@@ -334,6 +334,14 @@ def test_incremental_arguments(self, parser):
                 "No prefix id. " + _wrap(_tool("get_weather:0", '{"city": "NYC"}')),
                 id="no_functions_prefix",
             ),
+            pytest.param(
+                "Help. "
+                + _wrap(
+                    _tool("functions.invalid.0", '{"city": "Beijing"}'),
+                    _tool("functions.valid:1", '{"city": "Shanghai"}'),
+                ),
+                id="invalid_id_skipped",
+            ),
         ],
     )
     def test_streaming_matches_nonstreaming(self, parser, model_output):

@@ -904,6 +904,11 @@ def _events_to_delta(
                 case EventType.REASONING_START:
                     pass  # no delta-level effect
 
+        # Slots include calls rejected by name (never sent), which the
+        # non-streaming result drops. Stream each call at its position there.
+        for tc in tool_call_deltas:
+            tc.index = sum(slot.name_sent for slot in self._tool_slots[: tc.index])
+
         if len(tool_call_deltas) > 1:
             tool_call_deltas = self._coalesce_tool_call_deltas(tool_call_deltas)
